plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plane diagram in which one ellipse is shown against two superimposed coordinate systems. The standard frame consists of thin black double-headed arrows, a horizontal axis labeled x at its right end and a vertical axis labeled y at its top, meeting at the origin. Laid over them is a second pair of orange double-headed axes rotated counterclockwise about that same origin: the one running from lower left to upper right is labeled x', and the one running from lower right to upper left is labeled y'. The ellipse is a dark blue outline centered at the origin and tilted so that its long axis lies along the orange x'-axis and its short axis along the y'-axis; it crosses the black horizontal axis on both sides and extends above and below the black vertical axis. A small curved arc drawn between the positive x-axis and the positive x'-axis marks the rotation and is labeled theta. Neither set of axes carries tick marks or numeric values. Placing both frames on one picture invites a comparison between a point's coordinates in the original system and its coordinates in the rotated one. The figure motivates the treatment of conic equations that contain an xy term, which describe conics turned away from alignment with the coordinate axes.

interactionPlan.concept: A conic whose axes are tilted relative to the x,y axes picks up an xy cross term; rotating the coordinate frame by the tilt angle θ into x',y' aligns the axes with the conic and eliminates that term.
elements: Thin black double-headed horizontal axis with arrowheads at both ends, labeled 'x' at its right end
Thin black double-headed vertical axis with arrowheads at both ends, labeled 'y' at its top
Origin where both frames intersect (common center)
Orange double-headed axis running lower-left to upper-right, labeled x' in orange italic near its upper-right arrowhead
Orange double-headed axis running lower-right to upper-left (perpendicular to x'), labeled y' in orange italic near its upper-left arrowhead
Dark navy-blue ellipse outline centered at the origin, major axis along x', minor axis along y', unfilled
Small black curved arc between the positive x-axis and the positive x'-axis, labeled 'θ' in italic
Equation readout panel showing the conic in the currently selected frame (general form with Bxy term, or aligned standard form in x',y')
Highlight emphasis on the xy term / on the x'²,y'² terms depending on the selected frame
Clickable marker point on the ellipse (small filled dot)
Dashed black projection segments from the marker point to the x and y axes with foot-point ticks
Dashed orange projection segments from the marker point to the x' and y' axes with foot-point ticks
Two coordinate readout callouts near the marker: (x, y) in black and (x', y') in orange
Legend/key distinguishing the fixed black frame from the rotated orange frame
No tick marks or numeric labels on either axis set

interactions.teaches: That θ is the single angle measuring how far the conic's own axes are turned from the x,y axes; sweeping it turns the orange frame and the ellipse together, and only at the true tilt angle does the frame align with the ellipse.
interactions.label: Rotation angle θ

interactions.teaches: That the same ellipse has two algebraic descriptions: a messy Ax²+Bxy+Cy²=1 in the fixed frame and a clean x'²/a²+y'²/b²=1 in the rotated frame — the xy term is the algebraic signature of the tilt.
interactions.label: Equation frame

interactions.teaches: That a single physical point on the ellipse carries two different coordinate pairs, related by x'=x cosθ+y sinθ and y'=-x sinθ+y cosθ — the point never moves, only the ruler does.

demo_steps.title: Aligned conic: no tilt
demo_steps.narration: With θ = 0 the orange frame sits exactly on top of the black frame and the ellipse's major axis lies along x. The equation has no xy term.

demo_steps.title: Turn the conic away from the axes
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ upward: the ellipse and the orange axes rotate together while x and y stay fixed. As soon as θ ≠ 0 an xy term appears in the (x, y) equation and grows with the tilt.

demo_steps.title: Read the same conic in the rotated frame
demo_steps.narration: Switch the equation panel to the primed frame. The identical curve is now written as x'²/a² + y'²/b² = 1 — the cross term is gone because the axes match the ellipse.

demo_steps.title: One point, two coordinate pairs
demo_steps.narration: Click any point on the ellipse. Black dashed projections give (x, y); orange dashed projections give (x', y'). The point is unchanged — only the measuring frame differs.

demo_steps.title: Extreme tilt
demo_steps.narration: Push θ toward 90°: the ellipse's long axis swings onto the y-axis. The xy term shrinks back to zero at exactly 90°, showing the term measures misalignment, not shape.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The xy term in a conic's equation is not a property of the conic — it is a property of the coordinate frame; rotate the frame by θ and the term disappears while the curve itself never moves.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Square plane diagram, white background, origin centered. Fixed frame: thin black double-headed arrows spanning the full width and height, italic 'x' at the right end just below the axis, italic 'y' at the top. Rotated frame: two thicker orange (vermilion) double-headed arrows through the origin at angle θ and θ+90°, extending slightly beyond the black axes, labeled x' (upper right) and y' (upper left) in bold orange italic. Ellipse: dark navy outline, ~2 mm stroke, centered at origin, major-to-minor ratio roughly 2:1, major axis on x', large enough to cross the black horizontal axis on both sides and reach above and below the black vertical axis. A small black arc of radius about one-fifth the ellipse's semi-major axis sweeps from the positive x-axis to the positive x'-axis with an arrowhead, labeled italic θ just outside the arc. Equation panel in a corner, monospaced-ish math text; the xy coefficient term is highlighted orange when the original frame is shown, and the x'² / y'² terms highlighted orange when the rotated frame is shown. Clicked point: solid navy dot on the ellipse with black dashed drop-lines to x and y and orange dashed drop-lines to x' and y', plus two small readout labels (x, y) in black and (x', y') in orange. No tick marks or numbers anywhere on the axes.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rotating the coordinate frame by theta: the learner drags theta, the orange x' and y' axes turn with the ellipse while the black x and y axes stay fixed, showing how rotation removes the visual misalignment behind an xy term.
- Toggle between original and rotated equations: the learner switches from the x,y equation with the xy term to the x',y' equation aligned to the ellipse, and the active axes and equation terms highlight together to show why the rotated frame simplifies the conic.
- Click for coordinate comparison at a point: the learner clicks a point on the ellipse, projections to both axis systems appear with two coordinate readouts, making clear that the same point has different coordinates in the two frames.

authoredContext:
Until now, we have looked at equations of conic sections without an xy term, which aligns the graphs with the x- and y-axes. When we add an xy term, we are rotating the conic about the origin. If the x- and y-axes are rotated through an angle, say θ, then every point on the plane may be thought of as having two representations: (x,y) on the Cartesian plane with the original x-axis and y-axis, and (x ′, y ′) on the new plane defined by the new, rotated axes, called the x'-axis and y'-axis. See the figure.

The graph of the rotated ellipse x 2 + y 2 –xy–15=0

An ellipse centered at the origin, aligned with a rotated coordinate system (x', y') that is at an angle θ with respect to the standard (x, y) coordinate system.

We will find the relationships between x and y on the Cartesian plane with x ′ and y ′ on the new rotated plane. See the figure.

discrepancies: The generated figure adds a top-left equation panel (0.249x² − 0.328xy + 0.307y² = 1) and a two-entry legend ("fixed frame: x, y" / "rotated frame: x′, y′") that do not exist in the source; they are pedagogically useful but change the overall composition of the plate.

The θ arc in the source is a clean single arc spanning from the +x axis to the x′ axis with an arrowhead at the x′ end; in the render the arc/arrowhead reads as a small tick near the lower end and the θ glyph sits closer to the arc than the source's clearly offset label.

The ellipse in the source overshoots the visible axis extent (its ends are cut near the frame edges), while the generated ellipse sits comfortably inside the drawn axes, making it relatively smaller compared with the axis lengths.
Orange axis stroke weight and arrowhead size are somewhat lighter/smaller than the source's heavy orange double-headed arrows, so the orange frame is less visually dominant than in the original.
The 'y′' label is placed inside (to the right of) its arrow tip whereas the source places it just right of the tip along the axis; a minor placement shift only.
evaluation.notes: Structurally and conceptually an excellent reproduction — navy tilted ellipse, black fixed axes, orange double-headed x′/y′ axes and θ arc are all correct, with mathematically exact coefficient readouts and a rich, working set of interactions (θ slider, frame toggle, point probe, 5-step demo); the main deviations are added chrome (equation panel + legend) and a slightly under-scaled ellipse/orange axis weight relative to the source.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all scores are high (4.6 overall) with only minor cosmetic deviations, so further iteration is unnecessary.
